scope: synthetic dashboard/JSON workflows; no live Twilio or high-volume Groq calls

before.finding: Parent cgroup CPU throttling was hidden by Kubernetes reporting host CPU capacity. HPA adds pods, not physical CPU quota.

changes: Terminal checkpoint transition, cold archive and retirement now commit in one PostgreSQL transaction.
Existing minikube Docker container CPU quota raised to 4, preserving memory and volumes.
Actix upstream keep-alive changed from the default 5 seconds to 75, exceeding ingress-nginx's verified 60-second upstream idle timeout.
unchanged: Three API database connections per pod
Required synchronous acknowledgment from one replica
fsync, full_page_writes and synchronous_commit remain enabled
HPA minimum, maximum and cooldown policy
qualifications: Minikube refused to change the CPU count of an existing profile. The verified change used docker update --cpus=4 minikube instead; no cluster deletion was performed. Recheck actual Docker quota after future restarts.

The before-capacity PostgreSQL fault overlapped an image build and experienced control-plane contention/restarts. Retain its observations, but do not use its 134.929-second recovery as an isolated algorithm comparison.
The first four-CPU HPA run failed one incoming HTTP request with 502. All 8667 acknowledged creates, turns and hangups persisted. A failed unacknowledged creation is not acknowledged-data loss.

The first HPA run's strict all-iterations SQL audit failed because it included the unsuccessful creation. The supplementary acknowledged-ID audit records the valid consistency claim; availability remains failed.
Code, CPU allocation and connection settings are separate interventions. Combined final gains must not be attributed solely to Raft or terminal-transaction optimization.
